copy_detector.dev_ratio_def: RMS(speed_arm - v0) / RMS(speed_gt - v0). 0.0 = the arm commands NOTHING while the human did; 1.0 = it commands the same magnitude (says nothing about the sign — that is dev_r).
copy_detector.dev_r_def: Pearson r between (speed_arm - v0) and (speed_gt - v0) pooled over every (window, step) — the correlation of the DEPARTURE from the echo. copy_detector.echo_frac_where_human_acted_def: of the 1809 windows where the human's own speed departed from v0 by >= 0.5 m/s RMS, the fraction on which the arm nevertheless stayed within 0.1 m/s of v0. The discriminating subset: holding was demonstrably the wrong answer and the arm held anyway.

anti_echo._why_all_three: holdv0_baseline is the ADMISSIBILITY test (does the arm beat the copy, separated). copy_detector is the cheap always-on SCALAR (is the emitted plan literally the copy). shuffle_control is the FALSIFIER (does the plan follow a v0 we know to be wrong). The first can pass while the arm still copies on the subset that matters, the second cannot establish skill, and the third needs the model — so none of the three substitutes for another.

copy_detector.echo_index_def: fraction of windows with r(along, hold-v0) >= 0.999 AND mean |commanded accel| <= 0.1 m/s^2, JOINTLY. A pure hold-v0 planner scores exactly 1.0. Reported beside the GT's own value because most of this corpus genuinely is cruising; the EXCESS is the read.

copy_detector.dev_ratio_def: RMS(speed_arm - v0) / RMS(speed_gt - v0). 0.0 = the arm commands NOTHING while the human did; 1.0 = it commands the same magnitude (says nothing about the sign — that is dev_r).
copy_detector.dev_r_def: Pearson r between (speed_arm - v0) and (speed_gt - v0) pooled over every (window, step) — the correlation of the DEPARTURE from the echo. A pure hold-v0 planner has a nil departure, so this is UNDEFINED (dev_r_degenerate=true), which IS the signature. ⛔ The degeneracy gate is PHYSICAL (RMS <= 0.001 m/s), not `== 0`: the geometry recovers speed from norm(diff(positions))/dt and leaves a ~1.9e-06 m/s float32 residue, which an exact test correlated into a spurious dev_r = -0.0133 for a PURE ECHO.
copy_detector.echo_frac_where_human_acted_def: of the 2602 windows where the human's own speed departed from v0 by >= 0.5 m/s RMS, the fraction on which the arm nevertheless stayed within 0.1 m/s of v0. The discriminating subset: holding was demonstrably the wrong answer and the arm held anyway.

anti_echo._why_all_three: holdv0_baseline is the ADMISSIBILITY test (does the arm beat the copy, separated). copy_detector is the cheap always-on SCALAR (is the emitted plan literally the copy). shuffle_control is the FALSIFIER (does the plan follow a v0 we know to be wrong). The first can pass while the arm still copies on the subset that matters, the second cannot establish skill, and the third needs the model — so none of the three substitutes for another.

copy_detector.verdict_reason: echo_index_excess -0.1719 < 0.2: the arm is not measurably flatter than the human on these windows. ⚠️ CLEAN here is NOT an admissibility verdict — that is holdv0_baseline's job. This detector can only refute a copy, never establish skill.
copy_detector.echo_index_def: fraction of windows with r(along, hold-v0) >= 0.999 AND mean |commanded accel| <= 0.1 m/s^2, JOINTLY. A pure hold-v0 planner scores exactly 1.0. Reported beside the GT's own value because most of this corpus genuinely is cruising; the EXCESS is the read.
copy_detector.r_alone_is_not_the_detector: ⛔ both profiles are monotone ramps from the origin, so ANY forward-moving plan correlates ~1 with hold-v0 — a hard-braking planner still scores r ~0.99. r is a COMPONENT of echo_index, never a verdict on its own.
copy_detector.dev_ratio_def: RMS(speed_arm - v0) / RMS(speed_gt - v0). 0.0 = the arm commands NOTHING while the human did; 1.0 = it commands the same magnitude (says nothing about the sign — that is dev_r).
copy_detector.dev_r_def: Pearson r between (speed_arm - v0) and (speed_gt - v0) pooled over every (window, step) — the correlation of the DEPARTURE from the echo. A pure hold-v0 planner has a nil departure, so this is UNDEFINED (dev_r_degenerate=true), which IS the signature. ⛔ The degeneracy gate is PHYSICAL (RMS <= 0.001 m/s), not `== 0`: the geometry recovers speed from norm(diff(positions))/dt and leaves a ~1.9e-06 m/s float32 residue, which an exact test correlated into a spurious dev_r = -0.0133 for a PURE ECHO.
copy_detector.echo_frac_where_human_acted_def: of the 1809 windows where the human's own speed departed from v0 by >= 0.5 m/s RMS, the fraction on which the arm nevertheless stayed within 0.1 m/s of v0. The discriminating subset: holding was demonstrably the wrong answer and the arm held anyway.

anti_echo._why_all_three: holdv0_baseline is the ADMISSIBILITY test (does the arm beat the copy, separated). copy_detector is the cheap always-on SCALAR (is the emitted plan literally the copy). shuffle_control is the FALSIFIER (does the plan follow a v0 we know to be wrong). The first can pass while the arm still copies on the subset that matters, the second cannot establish skill, and the third needs the model — so none of the three substitutes for another.
anti_echo.\u26a0\ufe0f_context: admitting v0 removed an ARGUMENT, not a DEFICIT: MEASURED, vision + v0 sat at sigma/ADE 3.527 on the REF-C surface, still worse than a 0-parameter constant-yaw-rate rule at 1.1888.
